source: SPM Essay · Article, local cultural festival (older format, no trial paper named)
paragraphs: Last weekend, my class had the unforgettable opportunity to attend the annual local cultural festival—a vibrant celebration of our local heritage. Stepping into the festival grounds was like taking a journey back in time, offering us a profound experience of the traditions that define our community.

The festival was a feast for the senses. We witnessed a captivating performance of the Zapin dance, where dancers moved with grace and precision to traditional drums and flutes. The most engaging activity was the live demonstration of Batik Canting. A master artisan showed us how to draw intricate patterns onto cloth using hot wax, explaining the dedication and patience required for the craft. In another section, the air was filled with the delicious aroma of local delicacies. We watched a demonstration of cooking traditional Kuih, a craft passed down through generations. These main activities were highly engaging and demonstrated the authenticity of our local culture.

These types of festivals are fundamentally important in preserving the cultural identity of our community. By bringing traditional arts out into the open, the event acts as a vital link between the past and the present. It ensures that the knowledge and skills—like the complex patterns in the Batik or the steps of the Zapin—are not forgotten. When families attend together, the elders share stories and the youth become receptive to learning, strengthening their sense of belonging. The festival makes our unique identity visible and tangible, giving the community a cohesive sense of pride in its heritage.

To encourage young people to participate actively, we must make these events relevant and interactive. Firstly, organisers should incentivise attendance by offering special school-based credit or rewards for participation, perhaps through a cultural passport scheme. Secondly, incorporating technology is key; events could host a contest for the best TikTok video documenting the festival, or offer workshops where traditional crafts are combined with modern design. Finally, giving teenagers leadership roles—like being social media promoters or workshop assistants—will harness their enthusiasm and make them feel that they are the essential future of these traditions.

Attending the local cultural festival was a powerful reminder that our heritage is alive and beautiful. Through engaging activities and the commitment of the community, these events continue to serve as a critical shield against cultural loss. It is up to us, the younger generation, to participate, lead, and ensure that the spirit of our ancestors thrives for many years to come.
